title: Pendulum

slow_motion.evidence: No narration, captions, or on-screen text indicate slow motion; motion appears in real time.

subjects.description: small blue spherical pendulum bob swinging on a thin string from a fixed support

observation.what_happens: A blue ball suspended by a thin string swings back and forth as a pendulum below a fixed support. It starts held at the upper right, is released, and continues swinging freely through the end of the clip.

calibration.note: no ruler needed: the swing is measured as an angle

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth): hold g fixed and measure the pendulum's length L in metres from its swing
reasoning: Path is circular to 0.15 px and theta oscillates +-1.2 rad (~69 deg) with period ~2 s and amplitude decaying from 1.21 to 1.01, so large-angle geometry is needed and light damping matters. Candidates test small vs large angle and no damping vs linear viscous vs quadratic air drag to see what extrapolates best.

caveats: Length relies on Earth gravity being fixed, not measured from video scale.
Tiny tracking wobble remains, so damping is approximate for very long swings.
critique.finding: The ball swings as a pendulum with length {L} and light damping {gamma}. Gravity pulls it back while drag steals a little speed each swing.
critique.headline: Swinging ball loses a little energy with each swing.
critique.why_it_won: Linear drag keeps the swing size shrinking steadily while quadratic drag lets the later swings miss.

headline: Swinging ball loses a little energy with each swing.
finding: The ball swings as a pendulum with length 0.8 ± 2.93e-5 m and light damping 0.0601 ± 9.44e-5 1/s. Gravity pulls it back while drag steals a little speed each swing.

eyeball.law_in_words: pendulum obeys theta_ddot + gamma theta_dot + (g/L) theta = 0, so small-angle period T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) and amplitude envelope decays as exp(-gamma t/2); L from string length vs 1-m black-white scale bar and grid, gamma from slow decay of swing amplitude over several periods
